en: Points of Controversy The Great Fifty-Section The Twenty-third Chapter
The Discussion on the Unproduced:
Is form unproduced? Yes.

"Is form not impermanent, not conditioned, not dependently originated, not subject to destruction, not subject to vanishing, not subject to fading away, not subject to cessation, and not subject to change?
"One should certainly not say so...

"...is it not the case that form is impermanent, conditioned, dependently originated, subject to destruction, subject to vanishing, subject to fading away, subject to cessation, and subject to change?"
“Yes.
“If form is impermanent, conditioned,
and subject to change, then indeed, it should not be said:”
“Form is unestablished.
Is it suffering alone that is established? Yes.
But has it not been said by the Blessed One that "whatever is impermanent is suffering"— namely,
"form is impermanent"?
Yes, it has.
If that which is impermanent has been stated by the Blessed One to be suffering—
as in, "Form is impermanent"— then indeed, it should not be said that "only what is suffering is fully established" ... and so on.
Feeling … perception … volitional formations …
consciousness … the eye-base …pe… the mental-object-base …
The eye-element … the mental-object-element … the eye-faculty … [and so on] … up to … [the mind-faculty].
Is the faculty of one who has already known not yet fully accomplished?
Yes. Is the faculty of one who has already known not impermanent? ... [and so on] ... Yes.
Is it not subject to change?
One should not say so.
…pe… Is not the faculty of one who has fully known (aññātāvindriya) impermanent, conditioned, and subject to change?
“Yes.

“If the faculty of one who has already known (aññātāvindriya) is impermanent, conditioned, dependently arisen, subject to destruction, subject to vanishing, subject to fading away, subject to cessation, and subject to change, then indeed, sir,
it should not be said that ‘the faculty of one who has already known is unconditioned.’”
Is suffering alone fully established? Yes.
But has it not been said by the Blessed One that whatever is impermanent is suffering?
“Is the faculty of one who has already known impermanent?
“Yes.
“If that which is impermanent has been called suffering by the Blessed One—”
“The faculty of one who has already known is impermanent,” yet indeed,
it should not be said that “only what is suffering is fully established.
The discussion on the unestablished is finished.
The Twenty-third Chapter.
Its summary (uddāna) is:
Sexual intercourse should be practiced with a single intention; [the offense of] sexual intercourse with non-human beings by means of the praise of arahants.
They practice the Dhamma; the Bodhisatta goes to a state of ruin for the sake of exercising power according to his own will;
he enters a womb; he performs austerities; he practices self-mortification; he acknowledges another teacher;
there is that which is not lust but resembles lust; there is that which is not hatred but resembles hatred; there is that which is not delusion but resembles delusion.

There is that which is not a defilement but resembles a defilement; there is matter that is unconditioned (*aparinipphanna*); the faculty of one who has already known (*aññātāvindriya*) is unconditioned.
This is the Minor Section of Fifty Parts.
Its summary verse:
The new, extinction, and single intention.
This is the summary of the Fifties:
The Great Guide and the underlying tendencies.
The restraint with the "small" as the fifth;
the crushing of the doctrines of others,
established upon the root of the Suttas.
In the Teacher’s system,
the *Ujjotanā* consists of thirty-five recitation sections (*bhāṇavāra*) as the equipment for the *Kathāvatthu*.
The manual on the bases of discourse is completed.
